decision: Outfit as pieces by slot (top/bottom/over/head) + material, not one mesh per culture
why: 12 pieces dress every row and compose

decision: Work loops keyframed in code as offsets over pack clips
why: pack has no knapping/grinding/spinning clips; offsets reuse rotateWorld, cost no bytes, testable

decision: Tools, ornaments, caps as runtime primitives on bones
why: zero asset bytes; small at 120 px

decision: Garment pieces made from the bodies: shells of body triangles (fitted) and lathes with nearest-vertex weights blended with pelvis (hanging)
why: no CC0 clothing exists for this rig; shells bend exactly with the body; pelvis blend stops skirts splitting between legs
result: 26 files, 22-54 KiB each, total assets 1,677 KiB

decision: Hide body triangles under worn fitted pieces via a _COVER bitmask baked per body vertex
why: thin shells over an animated body let skin poke through; dropping covered triangles fixes it and draws less
result: no skin through parkas or trousers on the sheet

decision: A modelled atlas record (source: model) overrides only rows resting on unverified sources, never a checked row or other humans
why: first sheet: the atlas model put the Ice Age hunter in a short-sleeved hide tunic and the Neanderthal in trousers, overriding Gilligan 2010 and Collard 2016

decision: Head loads carried hands-free; props offset by each body's own bone positions
why: the woman's body is shorter, so a basket placed for the man floated; a raised steadying arm read wrong

decision: A long-sleeved top over trousers gets coat tails (skirt_short)
why: parka and coat over trousers read as a bodysuit

decision: Still frames show work at full strength; work and rest alternate only when animating
why: a still at a rest instant would hide the role

decision: Contact-sheet harness bundles the real viewer with esbuild (dev dep of footstep-generator/avatar) and synthetic people
why: finding 12 specific people on the map is slow and flaky; the spec and viewer are the same code
